title: Domains: per-year cost on longer terms; the registrant's confirmation followed until it's done
why: Jason, 2026-11-17: "we should show the per year costs for multiple year selections. Contact details must be captured and sent when purchasing, the verification process follows after the purchase right, so we need a worker to follow and communicate this until it is resolved." (1) A multi-year choice shows its cost a year beside the total and the renewal after ("$206.40 for 10 years ($20.64 a year; $24.99 a year after)"). (2) The registrant's details are already captured at checkout and sent on create; now the confirmation Name.com emails them (ICANN's rule; unconfirmed in about 15 days, the domain stops working) is followed: at registration the domain is marked waiting and its history says so; the 15-minute domains job asks Name.com which contacts are unconfirmed (GET /core/v1/contacts/unverified, live and sandbox apart), keeps each domain's deadline and email, and emails the owner at 13, 7, 3 and 1 days left; once Name.com no longer lists it, it's recorded as confirmed and the follow-up stops; if Name.com doesn't answer, nothing changes. The Domains tab shows Confirm the registrant with its due time (red within 3 days) and Send the confirmation again (POST /core/v1/contacts/verify/<id>:resend; Name.com's wait between sends is said plainly). Pulse opens 'Domain contact not confirmed' as Critical (Jason: "HIGH PRIORITY"; top of Pulse, 2-hour target) at 3 days left, with Send it again, Email the owner, and it closes itself when confirmed. The follow-up runs even with Domain sales Off (it only checks and reminds). Also: the domains page's date fallback threw 'Invalid option' in browsers (dateStyle with timeZoneName), which broke the History panel and would have broken the tab; fixed. The Domain sales 'Off' choice said bought domains still renew; corrected (auto-renew stops with it; they stay registered until their date). FAQ: why the registrant confirms.
